section_102.basis: 12-stage patent attack executed. No single patent teaches all four claim elements: (a) headache phenotype, (b) physiological trajectory, (c) failure-TYPE prediction, (d) salvage treatment selection. The specific combination is absent from all analyzed patents, their families, citations, and continuations.

section_103.basis: The combination of known elements creates a serious §103 threat:
known_elements: Biomarker-based patient selection for CSF diversion (US12151072B2 — RNFL → CSF diversion)
AI-based medical prediction and classification into categories (WO2024192175A1 — neural network → classification)
Phenotype-based VSS risk stratification (Lakhani 2026 — symptom phenotype → readmission risk)
Pressure-gradient response patterns predicting stent-adjacent stenosis (Daggubati 2019 / PMC6450594)
section_103.examiner_argument: An examiner COULD argue: 'It is known to use biomarkers for patient selection (US12151072B2), known to use AI for medical classification (WO2024192175A1), known to use symptom phenotype for VSS risk stratification (Lakhani 2026), and known to use pressure-gradient patterns to predict stent outcomes (Daggubati 2019). Combining these to predict VSS failure type is obvious.'
section_103.counterargument: The counterargument is that NONE of these references specifically: (a) distinguishes R2-C3 from R2-C1, (b) uses physiological TRAJECTORY (temporal evolution, not single-point measurement), (c) predicts WHICH failure phenotype (not just binary success/failure), or (d) selects a salvage treatment based on the predicted phenotype. The specific technical contribution — using physiological trajectory to distinguish pressure-independent headache (R2-C3) from pressure-dependent headache (R2-C1) — is NOT described in any combination of prior art.
section_103.uncertainty: The §103 threat is SERIOUS but NOT decisive. A patent attorney would need to evaluate whether the counterargument is strong enough to overcome the examiner's combination argument. This is INCONCLUSIVE.

exact_discriminator_analysis.question: What specific physiological input distinguishes R2-C3 from R2-C1 before either phenotype manifests?

candidate_discriminators.name: Baseline opening pressure (OP)
candidate_discriminators.hypothesis: Higher baseline OP → more likely R2-C1 (pressure-dependent); lower baseline OP → more likely R2-C3 (pressure-independent)
candidate_discriminators.evidence: Goodwin 2014: failures (shunt need, R2-C1) had OP 50 vs 37 cmH2O. Ahmed 2011: R2-C3 cases had 'normal pressures' (specific values not reported per-patient in abstract).
candidate_discriminators.testable: PARTIALLY — D'Amato has per-patient OP but 0 R2-C3 cases. Ahmed has 3 R2-C3 cases but per-patient OP not in public PDF.

candidate_discriminators.name: Trans-stenotic gradient (TSG)
candidate_discriminators.hypothesis: Higher TSG → more likely R2-C1 (mechanical stenosis is the driver, stenting should work but if OP is very high, stent may be insufficient); lower TSG → more likely R2-C3 (stenosis is not the primary driver, headache has non-venous cause)
candidate_discriminators.evidence: Ahmed (mean TSG 20 mmHg, 5.8% R2-C3) vs Midtlien (median TSG 14 mmHg, 57% group-level recurrence). But this cross-cohort comparison was RETRACTED in Round 56d (non-equivalent endpoints).
candidate_discriminators.testable: NO — no cohort has both per-patient TSG AND per-patient R2-C3 classification
candidate_discriminators.classification: CANDIDATE — not validated, cross-cohort comparison retracted

candidate_discriminators.name: Post-VSS OP change (early pressure trajectory)
candidate_discriminators.hypothesis: Patients whose OP normalizes rapidly after VSS → if headache persists, it's R2-C3 (pressure-independent). Patients whose OP does NOT normalize → R2-C1 (pressure-dependent).
candidate_discriminators.evidence: D'Amato: mean OP change 12.0 cmH2O (single-stent group). The 1 case with OP 40 post-VSS had persistent headache + papilledema = R2-C1 (NOT R2-C3). The 3 Ahmed R2-C3 cases had normal pressures post-VSS (Rickham reservoir confirmed).
candidate_discriminators.testable: PARTIALLY — D'Amato has post-VSS OP per-patient. But D'Amato has 0 R2-C3 cases (all headache persisters had elevated OP = R2-C1). Ahmed has 3 R2-C3 cases with confirmed normal post-VSS pressures, but per-patient OP trajectory not in public PDF.
candidate_discriminators.classification: STRONGEST CANDIDATE — the logical discriminator is: IF post-VSS OP normalizes AND headache persists → R2-C3. IF post-VSS OP does NOT normalize AND headache persists → R2-C1.
candidate_discriminators.key_insight: This discriminator requires WAITING until after VSS to measure post-VSS OP. It is NOT a pre-treatment predictor — it is an EARLY post-treatment classifier. The 'prediction time' is early post-VSS (days to weeks), NOT pre-treatment.

candidate_discriminators.name: Headache phenotype (ICHD-3: migraine vs tension-type vs MOH)
candidate_discriminators.hypothesis: Migraine phenotype → more likely R2-C3 (CGRP-mediated, pressure-independent). Tension-type → less discriminative.
candidate_discriminators.evidence: Ahmed 2011: 'Up to 68% of patients with IIH have other definable pressure-independent headaches.' No ICHD-3 classification in any VSS cohort.
candidate_discriminators.testable: NO — no open cohort has ICHD-3 headache classification + VSS outcome

candidate_discriminators.name: CGRP biomarker
candidate_discriminators.hypothesis: Elevated CGRP → more likely R2-C3 (CGRP-driven headache persists despite VSS)
candidate_discriminators.evidence: CGRP-IIH link established (Brain 2024, Headache 2024, Neurology 2024/2026). But no VSS cohort measures CGRP.
candidate_discriminators.testable: NO — no open cohort has CGRP + VSS outcome

strongest_discriminator.name: Post-VSS OP trajectory (early pressure normalization vs persistent elevation)
strongest_discriminator.logic: IF post-VSS OP normalizes (≤25 cmH2O) AND headache persists → R2-C3 (pressure-independent headache). IF post-VSS OP remains elevated (>25 cmH2O) AND headache persists → R2-C1 (pressure-dependent failure).
strongest_discriminator.why_this_is_the_strongest: It is the ONLY discriminator that: (a) has logical biological basis, (b) is supported by both D'Amato (R2-C1 case had OP 40 post-VSS) and Ahmed (3 R2-C3 cases had normal post-VSS pressures), (c) uses a measurement that IS available in clinical practice (post-VSS lumbar puncture), (d) changes the decision (R2-C1 → shunt; R2-C3 → headache-directed treatment).
strongest_discriminator.critical_limitation: This is NOT a PRE-treatment predictor. It requires post-VSS measurement. The 'prediction time' is EARLY POST-VSS, not pre-treatment. This means the invention would be: 'an early post-VSS diagnostic method that classifies headache persistence as pressure-dependent (R2-C1) or pressure-independent (R2-C3) based on post-VSS OP trajectory, enabling different salvage pathways.'
strongest_discriminator.decision_value_counterfactual: WITHOUT the classifier: when headache persists post-VSS, clinicians repeat LP and angiography. If OP is elevated, they offer shunt. If OP is normal AND no restenosis, they offer symptomatic treatment (no specific headache pathway). WITH the classifier: the same sequence is followed, but the classifier could AUTOMATE the decision and could potentially predict EARLIER (using OP trajectory rather than single-point measurement) whether the headache will be pressure-independent. The decision-value depends on whether the classifier can predict R2-C3 BEFORE the clinician would otherwise discover it through routine follow-up.
strongest_discriminator.classification: STRONGEST CANDIDATE DISCRIMINATOR — but decision-value is UNCERTAIN (may not change the decision if clinicians already measure post-VSS OP)

counterfactual_decision_value.question_1: Would knowing the prediction cause a different treatment than clinicians would choose without it?
counterfactual_decision_value.answer_1: UNCERTAIN — the strongest discriminator (D-3, post-VSS OP trajectory) requires a measurement (post-VSS LP) that clinicians ALREADY perform. The classifier would add value ONLY IF: (a) it predicts R2-C3 EARLIER than routine LP would reveal normal pressures, OR (b) it uses a trajectory (multiple OP measurements over time) rather than a single LP to make a more confident classification. Whether this temporal advantage changes outcomes is UNKNOWN.
counterfactual_decision_value.question_2: Does that different treatment improve the relevant outcome?
counterfactual_decision_value.answer_2: UNKNOWN — no study has compared 'early R2-C3 identification + headache-directed treatment' vs 'routine post-VSS follow-up + symptomatic treatment when headache persists'. The outcome improvement (reduced headache burden, improved quality of life, reduced unnecessary repeat procedures) is HYPOTHETICAL.
counterfactual_decision_value.classification: DECISION-VALUE = UNKNOWN — the counterfactual has not been tested

verdict.strongest_discriminator_identified: D-3: Post-VSS OP trajectory (early pressure normalization vs persistent elevation)
verdict.discriminator_classification: STRONGEST CANDIDATE — but NOT pre-treatment (requires post-VSS measurement)
verdict.overall_classification: DISCOVERY HYPOTHESIS — NOT promoted. The 12-stage patent attack found no direct anticipation, but the §103 threat is serious. The strongest discriminator (post-VSS OP trajectory) may not change decisions because clinicians already measure post-VSS OP. The invention frontier, IF IT EXISTS, is in the TEMPORAL advantage of trajectory-based classification over single-point measurement — but this has NOT been demonstrated.
verdict.predictor_discovery_gate: YELLOW / UNKNOWN — discriminator identified but not validated, decision-value unknown
next_moves: 1. The strongest discriminator (D-3, post-VSS OP trajectory) is NOT pre-treatment — it requires post-VSS measurement. This changes the invention framing from 'pre-treatment prediction' to 'early post-treatment classification'.

2. The decision-value is UNKNOWN — clinicians may already measure post-VSS OP, making the classifier redundant. Need to investigate whether trajectory-based classification adds value over single-point OP measurement.

3. The §103 threat is SERIOUS — the combination of known elements (biomarker selection + AI classification + phenotype stratification + pressure-gradient patterns) could be argued as obvious by an examiner.

4. Per Article XXXIV (stop coding when reality is the next bottleneck): the autonomous loop has reached the limit of what zero-cost analysis can establish. The next step requires EITHER: (a) per-patient data with post-VSS OP trajectory + R2-C3 classification, OR (b) a decision analysis showing that trajectory-based classification changes clinical decisions.
